docMeta.description: Industrial 4G LTE cellular router designed for energy sector substation automation. Supports all LTE bands including 450 MHz (B31/B72), Dual SIM with auto-fallback, TPM 2.0, and IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack. Features OpenVPN and IPSec VPN, dual APN for traffic separation, and integrated firewall. DIN-rail metal housing, 12–48 V DC input, high EMC immunity per EN 61000-4. Managed centrally via Smart EMS with zero-touch provisioning.

answerRationales.questionText:
Does the product process personal data?
Examples: address labels
answerRationales.rationale: The router processes account/network identifiers, logs, credentials and transported customer traffic or diagnostic packet captures. Network cameras are foreseeable connected equipment, so identifiable images may be carried and exposed if the router is compromised. Significant personal-data impact is a conservative scenario assumption; actual payload, sensitivity, volume and retention are unconfirmed.

answerRationales.questionText:
Does the product contain ACME Security's or your customers' intellectual property?
Note: Only IP which is part of / accessible by the firmware / software in the product is in scope of this question. Gaining access to optical and mechanical IP are not covered by this question (and the cybersecurity risk analysis)
answerRationales.rationale: Embedded router firmware, protocol/security implementations and any uploaded application code. Conventional routing/VPN functionality is assumed to have limited innovation value; no high-value customer algorithm or proprietary process logic is evidenced. Exact commercial IP value requires owner confirmation.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product contain credentials / cryptographic keys that allow access to sensitive data or to systems in the product's operational environment? (Note: this includes cryptographic data introduced by the customer.)
answerRationales.rationale: VPN keys/certificates and local or external-AAA credentials can grant access to router management and connected operational networks. Affected assets include router configuration, remote VPN/control systems and IED/RTU communications. Major disturbance assumes loss or misuse of this access disrupts field monitoring/control; fatal injury or plant destruction is not established by the manuals.

answerRationales.questionText:
Can a loss of availability of the product (or its communication) endanger the health of people?
(Consider how the operational environment reacts to a loss of availability of the product.)
answerRationales.rationale: Assessment scenario: interruption of IED/RTU monitoring/control communication can delay detection or response to unsafe field conditions. Potentially dangerous situation is an assumed deployment consequence; the router is not a safety function and independent interlocks, redundancy and fail-safe responses are unconfirmed. No life-threatening consequence is established by the manuals.

answerRationales.questionText: Can a manipulated product (or its communication) endanger the health of people? Also consider cases where the product is used against its intended use or misconfigured!
answerRationales.rationale: Assessment scenario: malicious routing, firewall or VPN changes, or altered operational traffic, could prevent correct monitoring/control or contribute to unsafe field operation. The potentially dangerous rating reflects the existing substation use case and foreseeable misconfiguration. Downstream command validation, independent safety safeguards and redundancy are unconfirmed; fatal injury is not established by the manuals.

answerRationales.questionText: Can a manipulated product disclose personal data to an attacker? Also consider cases where the product is used against its intended use or misconfigured!
answerRationales.rationale: A compromised router may expose account-linked identifiers, logs, packet captures and customer traffic. Network cameras are foreseeable connected equipment and can carry identifiable images. Significant impact assumes such images or other personal payload are accessible following compromise; actual data categories, scale and deployed encryption require confirmation.

answerRationales.questionText:
Can a manipulated product disclose intellectual property to an attacker? Also consider cases where the product is used against its intended use or misconfigured!

Note that this includes both ACME Security's and your customers' IP.
answerRationales.rationale: Embedded router firmware and uploaded application code; potentially customer network/configuration information carried in backups or diagnostics. The rating assumes conventional routing/security logic rather than a demonstrated highly innovative algorithm or substantial proprietary process data. Owner validation is needed for actual IP value.

answerRationales.questionText: Can a manipulated product disclose credentials / cryptographic material to an attacker? Also consider cases where the product does not disclose the material but misuses its access to other systems! (E.g., product contains access credentials to store data on a server.)
answerRationales.rationale: VPN certificates/private keys, pre-shared secrets, local administrator passwords and external-service/AAA credentials. Disclosure or misuse could give access to router configuration and operational networks, disrupt routing/VPN links or support further attacks on IED/RTU and remote management/control systems. Major disturbance is the retained deployment assumption; no fatal injury or plant destruction claim is inferred.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product support authentication at any level (e.g., RADIUS, logins, JWTs, session cookies, MAC Authentication Bypass)?
answerRationales.rationale: Router management credentials and session tokens (loal or external-AAA logins, RADIUS secrets, web/API sssions) could leak through unauthenticated access. Afected assets are these credentials and the account dentifiers they carry. Low personal-data impact is aconservative scenario assumption; no further persona data is evidenced on this path.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product maintain security logs?
answerRationales.rationale: Router security logs (authentication, configuration-cange and firewall/VPN events) could be manipulated s they are no longer trustworthy for diagnosis or incdent analysis. Affected assets are the security logsand the event history they provide. Disturbance assues the operator can restore trustworthy logging by rset or reconfiguration; no regulatory traceability rquirement is evidenced (QIE8 = No).

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product support wireless connections?
answerRationales.rationale: Cellular modem/client connecting over 2G/3G/4G carrier networks; SIM/APN settings and VPN endpoints are configured by administrators. SMS management is also documented. Optional hardware variants provide Wi-Fi access point/client functions. Exact variant and deployed service restrictions are unconfirmed; carrier access control alone does not establish trustworthy communicating peers.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product offer a configuration interface?
answerRationales.rationale: WebUI/CLI configuration requires local administrator credentials or configured external AAA; standard accounts are read-only. Configurable service enablement, source-IP/port ACLs, HTTPS/SSH and inactivity timeouts restrict access. This is a documented mechanism, not confirmation of the deployed settings; default credentials must be changed and insecure/exposed services restricted.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product communicate with an external system locally (e.g., a USB stick, an SD card, an RFID tag)?
answerRationales.rationale: SIM interfaces exchange subscriber/authentication data with the local modem. The serial console exchanges administration commands; variant-dependent RS232/RS485 and digital I/O may exchange field-equipment data or control signals. Optional interfaces and connected devices are not confirmed and are not assumed trustworthy. No USB or SD interface is inferred.

answerRationales.questionText: Does the product communicate with an external system on the Internet (e.g., an untrusted 3rd party backend, a vendor cloud service, a vendor server system)?
answerRationales.rationale: Remote VPN peers and control/management systems exchange operational traffic, routing information and VPN authentication material. Configured services may communicate with external AAA, DNS/DDNS, NTP, syslog, email and certificate/SCEP servers. Exact deployment and peer trust are unconfirmed, so external systems are treated as untrusted in the worst case.

Annex I, Part II: vulnerability handling requirements

identify and document vulnerabilities and components contained in products with digital elements, including by drawing up a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at the very least the top-level dependencies of the products;
entries.notes: Maintain a component inventory and a machine-readable SBOM (e.g. CycloneDX or SPDX) covering at least top-level dependencies, regenerated for every release.

entries.title: in relation to the risks posed to products with digital elements, address and remediate vulnerabilities without delay, including by providing security updates; where technically feasible, new security updates shall be provided separately from functionality updates;
entries.notes: Operate a remediation process with defined timelines; ship security fixes decoupled from feature releases where technically feasible.

entries.title: apply effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product with digital elements;
entries.notes: Establish a recurring security testing cadence (e.g. penetration tests, fuzzing, dependency scanning, code review) and record the results.

entries.title: once a security update has been made available, share and publicly disclose information about fixed vulnerabilities, including a description of the vulnerabilities, information allowing users to identify the product with digital elements affected, the impacts of the vulnerabilities, their severity and clear and accessible information helping users to remediate the vulnerabilities; in duly justified cases, where manufacturers consider the security risks of publication to outweigh the security benefits, they may delay making public information regarding a fixed vulnerability until after users have been given the possibility to apply the relevant patch;
entries.notes: Publish security advisories per fixed vulnerability: description, affected versions, impact, severity, and remediation steps. Delayed publication must be justified and time-bounded.

entries.title: put in place and enforce a policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure;
entries.notes: Adopt, publish and enforce a CVD policy (e.g. based on ISO/IEC 29147 and 30111).

entries.title: take measures to facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities in their product with digital elements as well as in third-party components contained in that product, including by providing a contact address for the reporting of the vulnerabilities discovered in the product with digital elements;
entries.notes: Provide a single, published point of contact (e.g. security@ address and security.txt) for vulnerability reports, covering third-party components.

entries.title: provide for mechanisms to securely distribute updates for products with digital elements to ensure that vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner and, where applicable for security updates, in an automatic manner;
entries.notes: Protect the update channel end-to-end (signed updates, integrity and authenticity verification on device); support automatic security updates where applicable.

entries.title: ensure that, where security updates are available to address identified security issues, they are disseminated without delay and, unless otherwise agreed between a manufacturer and a business user in relation to a tailor-made product with digital elements, free of charge, accompanied by advisory messages providing users with the relevant information, including on potential action to be taken.
entries.notes: Distribute security updates promptly and free of charge for the committed support period, accompanied by advisories with recommended user actions.

Scope of this version: EN 18031-1 (Article 3(3)(d)) and EN 18031-2 (Article 3(3)(e)) for internet-connected radio equipment. EN 18031-3 (Article 3(3)(f), equipment that transfers money, monetary value or virtual currency) is out of scope; such equipment needs a separate assessment. Applicability is decided by the answers: QA5 (wireless connections) with QA6 or QA10b (internet connection) for Part 1, and QI2 (personal data) in addition for Part 2. QA5 asks about wireless connections more broadly than radio equipment, so the product's radio role decides whether this framework applies. Each requirement shows the EN IEC 62443-4-2:2019 requirements its part's informative Annex B names; these links are shown and never change a verdict. It applies to radio equipment placed on the market between 1 August 2025 and 10 December 2027; Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/30 is repealed with effect from 11 December 2027 (Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/339).

treatments.treatmentRationale: Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to unauthorized configuration with planned human authentication, machine-certificate authentication. Build an interface-specific access matrix, enforce unique human credentials and applicable machine identities, and test local privilege bypass. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to remote-debug access with planned debug passwords and independent approval factor. Inventory enabled debug services, disable unnecessary ones and define unique credentials plus explicit approval-factor and bypass tests. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to password guessing with planned failed-login limiting. Scope the counter to every reachable IP login, document local alternatives and safe recovery, and test distributed guessing and lockout abuse. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to software compromise with planned secure development and vulnerability management. Inventory point-to-point protocols, isolate parser privileges and define malformed-input/exploit tests with vulnerability response criteria. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to customer-device attack with planned secure development and vulnerability management. Define forwarding and privilege boundaries between local devices and customer networks; test a compromised attached device and router context. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device exploit leading to customer-network DoS using the planned secure-development and vulnerability-management process. The connectivity and attack path remain in scope, so no avoidance is claimed. Define parser/exploit tests, forwarding limits, downstream containment and essential-traffic requirements; verify compromised-router flood behavior. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate product denial of service from untrusted local devices through a planned DoS/resource-isolation response. Specify per-interface resource quotas, essential-function priorities, alarms and recovery, and test floods on the local interface. Remove C20's unvalidated damage transformation; validate operational and safety consequences at system level. The Basic replacement plan claims no RAP or damage-reduction credit. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.
appliedMitigations: Planned denial-of-service resilience and resource isolation - verification pending

treatments.treatmentRationale: Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to unpatched-vulnerability exploitation; no agreed third-party risk transfer is claimed. Define manufacturer fix/support duties, operator release monitoring, patch deadlines, postponement restrictions and integrator advisory delivery. Record a receiving party and agreed handover if transfer is proposed later; retain manufacturer tracking meanwhile and verify update availability and each installation notification route. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to interception with planned authenticated encrypted communications. Define endpoint identities and sensitive-flow destinations; distinguish link eavesdropping from malicious authorized peers and test plaintext fallback. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to incoming-traffic manipulation with planned authenticated encrypted communications. Require per-command authorization and input validation alongside authenticated transport, then test a compromised but credentialed local peer. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to malicious update installation with planned authenticated encrypted communications, on-device update authenticity checks. Require manufacturer signatures verified on the router, reject modified packages, and test a malicious authenticated update sender and rollback policy. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to customer-device attack with planned authenticated encrypted communications, on-device update authenticity checks. Verify the update trust anchor and package checks, and specify downstream forwarding restrictions and pivot tests. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to customer-network denial of service with planned authenticated encrypted communications, on-device update authenticity checks. Test malicious authenticated update delivery and define outbound policing/resource separation protecting operational-network availability. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate the untrusted local-device path to IP disclosure with planned authenticated encrypted communications, on-device update authenticity checks. Document why firmware/IP trust still merits mitigation, then test independent signature verification and constrain firmware/backup read access. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

Mitigate local-link disruption through a planned local-network-continuity response. Distinguish router resource exhaustion from cable, switch or shared-network failure; define upstream resilience, alarms, independent alternatives and safe local behavior. Test representative link-loss and recovery scenarios. Remove C20's unvalidated damage transformation. The Basic replacement plan claims no RAP or damage-reduction credit. The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

The current rating is provisional; use the recalculated risk register. Trace implementation and validation in the next revision; release/deployment requires evidence and accountable owner review.

conditions.name: SDR 2.4 – Secure production
conditions.description: ACME Security's products are produced in a secure operational environment.

conditions.name: SDR 2.5 – Secure supply chain
conditions.description: ACME Security's suppliers are trustworthy and their products are not manipulated. The suppliers provide updates when needed.

conditions.name: SDR 3.2 - Update notifications reach the operator through the integrator
conditions.description: The product does not notify its users of available security updates by itself. The integrator passes the vendor’s advisories and update notifications to the operator of each installation, so that the party who schedules the update learns that one exists. Where the integrator has handed the installation over, the obligation passes with it.

conditions.name: SDR 1.12 – Product inaccessible
conditions.description: The product is installed in a physically inaccessible place. It is difficult for an attacker to gain physical access to the product.
conditions.rationale: The operator is responsible to limit access to the product and its physical interfaces taking adequate measures.

conditions.name: SDR 3.1 - Security updates are installed under the operator’s patch management
conditions.description: Security updates are not installed by the product on its own. The operator schedules them under its own patch management, decides when a release is installed, and may postpone one it cannot take yet — which is what a professional or industrial environment requires and what CRA Annex I (c) allows to be arranged elsewhere where automatic installation is not expected (Recital 56). The operator keeps a process that installs security updates within a defined period of their release.
